plan: For capital preservation, sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
This significantly reduces overall portfolio leverage and risk.
The remaining portfolio will be focused on income and broad index exposure.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, leading to lower expected drawdowns. Returns will be modest, prioritizing stability.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to reduce overall leverage.
Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Buy XLF at 4% to add diversification outside of tech/chips.
This plan balances growth potential with a focus on risk management.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month by reducing leverage and diversifying. It aims for risk-first growth, blending broad index with quality tech and some leveraged exposure. Expect moderate drawdowns.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to lean into growth.
Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Buy XLF at 6% to add diversified exposure from a strong scanner setup.
This plan uses leverage and concentration for aggressive growth potential.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month by increasing leveraged ETF exposure and concentrating in high-scoring setups. This strategy significantly raises both upside and drawdown potential. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and strict stop discipline is crucial to manage rapid losses.
